scope: Workers Free plan; isolated catevia-free-feasibility Worker; no Catevia credentials, users, database, or production route
plan: Workers Free: 100,000 requests/day and 10 ms CPU per invocation
source: wrangler tail JSON piped through collect-tail-metrics.mjs; load.mjs driving the probe over the public Internet from Viet Nam

load.note: cost-12 hash plus compare in one Durable Object
cost-12 hash plus compare across 10 synthetic shards

frontHttpWorker.note: This is the execution model the Free 10 ms CPU cap applies to.

durableObjectAuthCpuProbe.note: Durable Object invocations are not bounded by the Free 10 ms CPU cap; this is where password hashing runs.

conclusions.frontWorkerCpuHeadroom: about 10x: p95 1 ms against a 10 ms cap
conclusions.shardingBenefit: Durable Object wall p50 3452 ms single object vs 1220 ms across 10 shards, about 65 percent lower
conclusions.intermittent500SampleSize: 40 Durable Object invocations and 60 HTTP requests, all successful
conclusions.reliabilityCaveat: The 2026-09-24 record lists intermittent unexplained HTTP 500s under concurrent bcrypt load. They did not reproduce here, and a clean small sample does not close that reliability question.
conclusions.supersedes: The earlier reading that /api/auth/login exceeded the Free CPU cap came from a per-invocation cpuMs field in one tail sample. The aggregated front-Worker CPU for the same class of work is 0-1 ms.

remainingFreePlanRisks: 100,000 requests/day cap with no measured 24 hour production request baseline
